newsitem.title: LATVIA: Key Latvian government parties to meet over PM.
newsitem.headline: Key Latvian government parties to meet over PM.

text.p: The three key Latvian government parties of the Baltic state's eight-party coalition said on Thursday they would meet to discuss whether to recall Prime Minister Andris Shkele to his post or choose another premier.
Support for the return of Shkele as prime minister has grown but his recall is not certain, politicians said.
Shkele quit on Monday after President Guntis Ulmanis called on parliament to reject Shkele's choice of finance minister.
The meeting of the three largest parties will be held on Saturday. The largest party in parliament, the Democratic Party Saimnieks, has already said it wants Shkele back as premier.
But the position of the second-largest party, Latvia's Way, is unclear after the third party, Fatherland and Freedom, named its own candidate for prime minister.
Fatherland and Freedom's candidate is current economy minister Guntar Krasts.
Latvia's Way parliament faction leader Andrej Panteleev said his party was ready to discuss Krast's candidature.

"We have accepted Fatherland and Freedom's proposals to discuss the composition of a government led by Guntar Krasts but nothing is a priori excluded, even the candidature of Andris Shkele," he told Reuters.
As well as Saimnieks' support, Shkele also has the backing of some smaller government parties. But he has not yet said openly whether he is prepared to be nominated again.
Vassily Melnik, the finance minister who caused the row between Ulmanis and Shkele, himself quit yesterday, saying he was unhappy with all the turmoil his appointment had caused.
Ulmanis called on parliament to reject Melnik as Melnik had been investigated by the prosecutor's office under anti-corruption laws, although the office later said it found no wrongdoing.
